title: Resting Aging Joints Makes Them Worse
hook: The instinct when joints ache is to use them less. That's backwards — cartilage has no blood supply and depends on movement to get fed.
key_points: Aging wears down the cartilage and lubricating fluid that protect joints.
Avoiding movement accelerates the problem rather than sparing the joint.
Movement nourishes cartilage and strengthens the muscles that offload the joint.
Exercise can reduce osteoarthritis pain, not just preserve function.
Low-impact options: swimming, cycling, tai chi, yoga, walking on varied terrain.
content_html: Joints wear over time. The cartilage cushioning them thins, and the fluid that lubricates them changes. The natural response — use the joint less, protect it — turns out to make things worse.
extra_html:
Cartilage has no blood supply of its own. It gets its nutrients from the joint fluid around it, and that fluid circulates when the joint moves and is loaded. A joint that sits still is a joint that isn't being fed. On top of that, the muscles around a joint act as shock absorbers, taking load the cartilage would otherwise bear; let those weaken and every step puts more stress on the part that's already worn.

The practical version is gentler than it sounds. Low-impact activity does the job: swimming, cycling, tai chi, yoga, and walking on varied ground — the last with the bonus of training balance. And the effect isn't only preservation. Exercise has been shown to reduce osteoarthritis pain, which is the outcome people actually care about. Even a few minutes of the right kind of movement counts, which is a much lower bar than most people assume they need to clear.

related.title: Exercise Helps Hip Arthritis Less Than You'd Hope
related.hook: Exercise therapy is standard advice for hip osteoarthritis. A major review found the average benefit is small — and nobody yet knows which exercises work best.

related.title: Staying Strong as You Age
related.hook: The decline we associate with old age is partly the result of doing less. Staying active — in four distinct ways — keeps you independent far longer.

related.title: Move More, Sit Less
related.hook: Even if you hit the gym, hours of unbroken sitting carry their own health risk. Breaking up the day with movement matters as much as the workout.

flashcards.prompt: Why is resting a stiff, aging joint often the wrong instinct?

choices.text: Movement nourishes cartilage and strengthens the muscles protecting the joint
Rest causes cartilage to grow back too quickly and unevenly
Joints only hurt when they are fully rested

flashcards.explanation_html: Avoiding movement makes matters worse. Exercise helps nourish cartilage, builds the muscles that protect the joint, and can reduce osteoarthritis pain.

flashcards.prompt: Name three low-impact activities suggested for aging joints.
flashcards.back_html: Swimming, cycling, tai chi, yoga, and walking on varied terrain — the last also improves balance and mobility.
